topic: How does beam steering affect polarization purity and interference mitigation in congested multi-satellite scenarios?
consensus_response: Beam steering affects polarization purity and interference mitigation by introducing spatial filtering effects, causing imperfect orthogonality between adjacent beams. This leads to increased inter-beam interference (IBI), degrading system performance. To mitigate IBI, frequency channelization can enhance carrier-to-interference levels by dividing the frequency band into smaller sub-bands. Moreover, employing orthogonal polarizations between adjacent beams and adaptive array processing techniques can reduce interference. Adaptive array processing dynamically adjusts antenna weights based on real-time channel state information, optimizing beamforming and interference cancellation in congested multi-satellite scenarios.
